#/properties/original.rationale: The ground rules keep the message as written alongside its encoding, so nothing the operator dropped (punctuation, case, digits) is lost to the record.

#/properties/encoded.rationale: Ciphers see only A-Z. The encoding stands in for the Morse-era operator step: spaces as X or spelled out, numbers spelled out, important punctuation spelled or omitted. Morse itself is not emulated yet.

#/properties/separator.rationale: Operators used one convention per message (README ground rules), and the convention depends on the machine: no single space marker works for every cipher. The operator that prepared the message sets it. Ciphers never read it.
#/properties/separator.history: German Enigma traffic used X between words and as a full stop. M-209 operators keyed Z for a space, and the machine printed every Z as a space in decipher mode, so readers decided by experience which Zs were real letters.
